children: none, because the instrument is one comparison of two numbers that already exist - a stat plus a read of /proc/locks against a pid liveness already writes. There is no second mechanism hiding under it, which is exactly what distinguished it from a-beat-costs-what-changed, cast minutes earlier, where two mechanisms did hide under one number.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the_beater_holds_the_claim) -> PROVED -> [SUPERSEDED]

watchme.trigger: every beat - the probe rides the pulse it is about. Two reads (a stat plus one small file) add nothing measurable to a beat that currently costs seconds, and it needs no clock of its own, which is the point of berthing it here.
watchme.enough: NOT satisfied by a green on a healthy host - that is the state the incident already looked like from outside. Enough when it has seen the induced mismatch go loud AND has survived one real loop restart (the moment the pid legitimately changes, the obvious false-positive shape and the one thing that would teach an operator to ignore it).
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying BOTH pids, the lock's inode, and which of the three outcomes was seen - so a red arrives already saying which condition it is, rather than needing the host inspected while it is still true.
watchme.nexus: the ground_loop device's own tree - a fact about the heartbeat's identity, the same nexus its liveness and residency watches teach.
watchme.consumer: the trouble lane on a mismatch (the permanence half of Law 7 - the record must outlive the condition, because the condition's evidence is exactly what died last time), and the ground_loop pane for the standing answer.
